manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the green orange and place it in the bowl.

Task description: The target is the green-and-yellow orange on the table. Place it inside the light-blue bowl.

Success criteria: The green orange rests securely inside the bowl and is supported by it; the gripper is open and no longer holding the fruit.

## Execution tips

- Place the pads on opposite, fuller sides around the middle of the orange, with an opening slightly wider than its width there. Avoid the curved top and lower edge close to the table to reduce slipping or table contact.
- The green orange is partly obscured by fingers in the close view. Before closing, use the other view to confirm the fingers are on opposite sides of the fruit rather than mistaking image overlap for enclosure.
- When carrying the fruit, keep its base and the fingertips high enough to clear the bowl rim. Make pose adjustments in an open area outside the bowl to reduce brushing the rim.
- Bring the orange inside the bowl opening and near its supporting surface before slowly releasing. Watch clearance between opening fingers and bowl walls to reduce bouncing out or pushing the bowl.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start this real-robot episode with the specified parameters and act on the returned manual and live observations. When finished or unable to continue, I will call finish_episode and report the observed result and recording directory.

I have read the manual and confirmed the target is the green-yellow orange and the container is the light-blue bowl. I am adjusting the approach pose at height. Before closing, I will confirm fingers on both orange sides and check grasp security after lifting.

The target and bowl locations have been identified through the wrist camera. The gripper is still above the table and is moving forward in stages while adjusting its pose downward. I will shorten the steps near the fruit and check the clearance incrementally.

The gripper is above the target, and the orange remains in its original position. I am adjusting the downward grasp angle while leaving movement clearance based on joint feedback, then will descend in small steps to align with the middle of the fruit.

The gripper is approximately downward, with measured opening around 79 mm and the target centered between the fingers in view. Next I will descend at most 1 cm per step and close only after confirming the pads are beside the fruit.

Both cameras show that the orange has not been bumped and clearance on both sides of the gripper remains adequate. I am approaching the top of the fruit and continuing downward in small steps toward the side grasp position.
The close-range view shows a remaining front-back offset. I am correcting it in 1 cm steps. The gripper remains open, and no grasp has been attempted yet.
Both fingers are now on opposite sides of the orange, with the fingertips clear of the table. I will narrow the gripper slightly first, then check contact based on the measured opening and image.

The orange has left the table with the gripper, with measured opening around 58 mm, and remained between the fingers after two small lifts. I will first raise it enough to clear the bowl rim, then move toward the bowl.

The orange remained stable after being lifted and moved sideways, and its bottom is now above the tabletop objects. I am approaching the light blue bowl; once its rim is visible again at close range, I will align precisely.

The light blue bowl is in the wrist-camera view, and the orange remains securely grasped. I am maintaining clearance above the rim and aligning with the center of the opening; I will return to small movements when entering the opening.
The orange remains stable and has not been released. I am aligning horizontally with the bowl opening in steps of no more than 1 cm, while checking clearance between the fruit, fingers, and rim.
The orange is above the edge of the bowl opening, with a gripper gap of about 57.5 mm. It still needs a short lateral movement toward the bowl center, then I will lower by centimeters.
The orange is inside the bowl opening and is approaching the center while descending slowly. Neither the bowl nor grasp has visibly changed; the fruit has not been released.

Left-right alignment is complete, and I am lowering in centimeter steps above the bowl center. The orange remains supported by the gripper; next I will approach the interior support surface and open the gripper gradually.
The orange is inside the bowl opening, and a gap remains visible between the bowl wall and fingers. I am lowering further to reduce the drop distance after release.

The gripper is open to a measured width of about 66 mm. The orange has landed in the bowl and stopped visibly wobbling. Next I will lift the gripper away in small steps, confirming the fruit remains in the bowl and is no longer held.

After lifting the gripper away and waiting, the orange remains stable inside the bowl; the gripper is open and separated from it. Based on live observations, I judge the stated conditions satisfied. I will now end this episode; the on-site operator will confirm the final result.
